title: Dynamic headroom allocator and tenant safety profiles for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-level PRD for a Dynamic Headroom Allocator (DHA) that maintains per-tenant 'safety headroom' on Dedicated capacity pools to enable predictable low-latency bursts while improving overall utilization. This feature pairs an allocator with tenant-configurable safety profiles (priority tiers, burst credit behavior, prewarm hints) and makes allocation zone-aware to avoid correlated exhaustion. The allocator exposes admin controls and runtime observability hooks in Console and integrates with existing autoscale and fallback policies.
goals: Reduce tail latency for short bursty traffic by guaranteeing short-term headroom for tenants with safety profiles
Increase overall GPU utilization of Dedicated pools by reclaiming unused static buffer while preserving SLOs
Provide tenant controls for burst behavior (max burst rate, replenishment cadence, prewarm hints) and admin guardrails
Make allocation zone-aware to avoid cross-AZ correlated preemption and reduce blast radius
non_goals: Full rewrite of scheduler or replacement of existing preemption logic
Fine-grained per-request pricing changes (billing will use existing metering surface)
Supporting on-prem air-gapped customers in initial rollout (later phase)
user_personas: Platform engineer at a SaaS customer who needs consistent 99th percentile latency for interactive features
Redwood SRE responsible for Dedicated pools and SLA enforcement
Account manager for enterprise customers wanting control over burst policies
requirements: Allocator must reserve configurable short-term headroom per tenant expressed as GPU 'slots' or equivalent capacity units
Headroom must be zone-aware: allocator should not reduce global pool by more than a configured fraction in any single AZ
Safety profiles must include: priority tier (P0/P1/P2), max_burst_capacity, replenishment_window, prewarm_signal (boolean), and emergency_eviction_threshold
Prewarm hints: API for customer to tag certain workloads with prewarm=true; prewarm requests should trigger a best-effort pre-allocation within configured headroom
Allocator must integrate with autoscaler: if sustained load exceeds headroom, autoscaler takes precedence and scales Dedicated pool per existing policy
Observable metrics: per-tenant headroom_allocated, headroom_used, burst_credit_balance, prewarm_trigger_count, headroom_evictions, headroom_replenishments
Console UX: new Dedicated pool tab showing headroom heatmap by zone and tenant, and per-tenant safety profile editor
APIs & controls: admin API to override headroom, and customer-facing API to request soft-reserve and query burst_credit_balance
Fallback behavior: on headroom exhaustion, requests follow existing fallback policies (model variant fallback, cross-pool routing)
Backward compatibility: existing Dedicated customers with no safety profile should see no change in default scheduling or quotas
ux_constraints: Safety profile editing must be role-restricted in Console (only org-admins and platform-admins)
Heatmap must render cell counts for zones up to 128 tenants without UI degradation
API responses must be consistent with current rate-limiting headers and not add blocking latency
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Prefer short-term soft reservations over hard reservations to balance utilization vs. guarantees — chosen to protect utilization while retaining predictable burst behavior
Zone-aware allocation will slightly reduce theoretical maximum headroom per tenant but significantly reduce correlated failures during AZ storms
Prewarm hints are best-effort and can cause transient extra cost; customers must opt-in to avoid unintended allocation
metrics_and_success_criteria: Reduce median request cold-start latency for bursty tenants by >= 25% in first 2 minutes of a spike
Keep 99th percentile latency for targeted tenants within 1.5x of their baseline during bursts at least 90% of the time
Improve Dedicated pool GPU utilization by at least 8% in pilot customers after reclaiming unused static buffer
No increase in P0 incidents caused by allocator logic in rollout window (first 90 days)
Console adoption: 3 pilot customers configure safety profiles and use prewarm in first 60 days
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end flow: tenant safety profile created in Console, headroom_allocated metric appears, tenant can perform a soft-reserve request and consume burst credits
Zone safety: when subjected to a synthetic AZ spike in staging, allocator does not allocate more than configured zone_fraction per AZ
Observability: metrics documented; dashboards and alerting runbooks added and linked in tickets
Autoscaler interaction: sustained load above headroom triggers autoscaler scaling events per existing policy without allocator deadlock
Fallback: when headroom exhausted, requests are routed according to existing fallback rules and SLA degradation is within acceptable bounds
Security: admin override API requires admin role; tests for RBAC enforced in Console and API
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal staging): implement allocator and safety profile storage; smoke tests with synthetic tenants
Phase 1 (pilot, 1-3 customers): enable for two non-critical enterprise tenants in a single region with monitoring and manual rollback
Phase 2 (expanded pilot): add zone-aware policy tuning and Console UX; up to 10 customers across two regions
Phase 3 (general availability): enable self-serve safety profiles with defaults and guardrails; open to all Dedicated customers
Rollback criteria: increase in P0 incidents attributable to allocator, or sustained >10% SLA miss in pilot tenants
qa_and_tests: Unit tests for allocator logic and safety-profile parser
Integration tests validating autoscaler handoff under sustained load
Chaos tests: simulate AZ outage and verify zone_fraction invariants
Load tests: synthetic burst patterns to validate replenishment windows and headroom exhaustion behavior
Security tests: RBAC enforcement for Console and admin API endpoints
dependencies: PM-834001 (pricing review for prewarm best-effort costs)
open_questions: Should replenishment be purely time-based or include usage-weighted replenishment? (Tradeoffs: predictability vs. fairness)
Default safety profile values for newly created Dedicated pools — conservative by default or aggressive?
Approach to billing prewarm boons: show estimated potential extra cost to customer before enabling prewarm?
